messages.subject: Merging studies from different years
parts:
Hi,

I've got data from two studies with the same format- one carried out in 2013 and the other in 2019. I want to merge them together so as to get the input for unmarked. 

The way I have tried to do is that I've combined the camera operation matrices and then removed columns with all NAs. And use this and the merged species RT from both studies as the input for obtaining detection histories for individual species. But this leaves me with the error:
Error in camOp[i, as.character(record_dates_tmp[which_tmp])] : subscript out of bounds

I'm unsure how to correct this error.

Also, is this the correct way to approach this? I am able to obtain species detection histories from both studies separately and then combine them to use as the input for unmarked and this works fine. But I'm aiming to run a metadata analysis from multiple studies with the same data collection format, so its easier to merge them as raw data and then obtain detection histories as I'm also running it for multiple species.

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Merging studies from different years
parts:
Hi, 
and sorry for the late reply. Can you please share the code you used that led to the error? Right now I don't even know which function caused it. 
You can specify a season / session in the camera trap table and then pass that to cameraOperation() with the argument sessionCol. That was intended for such situations, combining data from multiple season (at the same locations). 
Please see vignette 3 for details: 
https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/articles/camtrapr3.html#multi-season-occupancy-analyses

If the studies were carried out at different locations (they don't have the same camera trap stations) then you can simply rbind() the camera trap tables and the record tables and then continue with cameraOperation / detectionMatrix. In that case you can e.g. include a "year" covariate in the models to account for the differences between the studies. 

Best,
Jürgen
